Written by
Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®

For house buyers in Salmon River and the rest of Langley, I check the permits, zoning and lot rules with you before you firm up. I've been a REALTOR® since 2015 and a member of the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board's Medallion Club for 10 straight years, which puts me in the top 1% of all Realtors in the Fraser Valley by FVREB sales. I have more than $500M in sales.

In Paragon, the MLS® system used by local REALTORS®, Salmon River is Langley sub-area F64. This feed pulls only Salmon River detached houses, so you won't see its townhomes, condos or acreages here. The sections below cover a rural district with houses mixed in, streams and setbacks and wells, septic and records, plus the checks I run before you write an offer.

blocks.text: A rural district with houses mixed in

parts.t: Salmon River is part of the Township of Langley's rural area, and its land use is guided by the Township's Rural Community Plan. Most of the district is farmland, hobby farms and acreage, with houses scattered along the country roads between them. A house listing here can still sit on a good-sized lot, so read the lot size on every listing rather than assuming it's a small town lot.
If you want the bigger parcels, my
Salmon River acreages and farms
page lists them. If you'd rather compare detached homes across the whole Township, see
all Langley houses for sale

The Salmon River itself and the creeks that feed it run through the district. The Township's streamside protection rules can limit where you build near a watercourse, and that matters if you plan an addition, a garage or a shop. Before you write an offer, I look at where the nearest stream sits on the property and what setback could apply. On some lots the usable yard is smaller than the lot lines suggest.

Many houses in Salmon River are on a private well and a septic system rather than municipal water and sewer. The Township's groundwater page explains the provincial rules for well users, and owners can join its Private Well Network.

For any house on a well, ask the seller for recent water test results and the well record if there is one, and plan for a flow test during your conditions. For septic, ask when the tank was last pumped and get an inspection. The Township's building records search can provide past permits and a site plan, which often shows where the well, tank and field sit.

Much of Salmon River is in the Agricultural Land Reserve. Look up every address on the Agricultural Land Commission's ALR map before you plan around a suite, a second home or a business. Land in the ALR comes with housing limits set by the ALC, and those rules can be stricter than Township zoning alone. If a house is in the ALR, I confirm what the ALC and the Township allow on that parcel before you rely on it.

Schools in and near the district include Coghlan Fundamental Elementary, Peterson Road Elementary and D.W. Poppy Secondary. Each address has a set catchment, and rural catchments can cover a wide area, so check every address with the Langley School District's catchment maps. Some rural families also look at bus routes, since walking to school isn't always practical out here.

Buyers who look at Salmon River houses usually want space and quiet without taking on a full farm. Some want room for a large garden, a workshop or a few animals where zoning allows. Others are moving out from Walnut Grove or Willoughby and want to stay close to Highway 1. Because the houses vary so much, two listings on the same road can need very different checks.

I check streamside setbacks, servicing and ALR status on every house you're serious about, and I pull the permit history before you write. If a listing mentions a suite, a shop or an outbuilding, I confirm it was permitted. I'll also show you recent sales of similar rural houses so your offer is based on more than the list price. 1. Does this page show Salmon River acreages?
No. It shows listings coded as houses. My Salmon River acreages and farms page lists properties coded as acreage.
2. Are there stream setbacks in Salmon River?
Many properties are near watercourses, and the Township's streamside protection rules can limit building near them. Check the setbacks before you plan an addition or a shop.
3. Do Salmon River houses use wells?
Many do. Confirm servicing for each address, and ask for water test results and the well record if the house is on a well.
4. Is Salmon River land in the ALR?
Much of it is. Check each address on the ALC's ALR map, because ALR land has its own housing limits.
5. What plan covers Salmon River?
The Township of Langley's Rural Community Plan guides land use in the district.
6. Which schools are near Salmon River?
Coghlan Fundamental and Peterson Road Elementary, and D.W. Poppy Secondary, are among the nearby schools. Confirm catchments for each address.
7. Can I get past permits for a Salmon River house?
Yes. The Township's building records search can provide past permits and site plans, which often show the well and septic locations.
